headers:
Will the City allow a separate, onetime startup / transition cost line item in the price proposal (e.g., for recruitment, initial
training, systems configuration, and policy implementation), or does the City expect all startup costs to be amortized into the
fixed and variable rates? If separate, in which section or tab of Attachment G should these costs be shown?

Start-up costs should be included in the Year 1 (2026-2027) column. A Start-up line is
provided in the Fixed overhead expenses category.
sample:
The Scope states that “unproductive downtime shall not be billed to the City” for paratransit where there are large gaps
between trips. Could the City please provide historical data (by month for the past 12–24 months) on paratransit driver
downtime exceeding one hour, so bidders can accurately forecast non‑billable time and related staffing needs?

This data is not readily available. Please see response to RFP questions 158 for details
on this provision.

The SOW shows significant training requirements: CDL, defensive driving, elder abuse, human trafficking, cybersecurity, First
Aid/CPR, etc. Will the City provide historical annual training hours per operator and per supervisor, as well as any minimum
annual retraining expectations, to support accurate budgeting for paid training time and trainer resources?

In the SOW, it is noted that the City covers repairs, major components, and maintenance, while the contractor is “financially
responsible for correcting any damage and paying for related expenses caused by the negligent maintenance or operation of
equipment or vehicles by Contractor's personnel,” and may be liable for repairs that Will otherwise have been covered under
warranty. Could the City clarify how preventable vs non‑preventable vehicle damage will be determined? Could a 2 year history
of accident repair costs be provided?

The operator is expected investigate each accident and determine if it was
preventable or not preventable. If the Contractor could have avoided an accident it is
considered preventable, If the accident occurred due to circumstances the contractor
could not control it is considered non-preventable. Historical accident repair data is
not available.
